item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Left Edge Sneaker Stays Visible

turns.text: Make this square for my shop. The shoe's way over on the left, so don't just crop the middle. Keep the whole shoe; plain padding to match the background is fine if needed. No other edits.

item.tests: Tests subject-aware reframing of an off-centre product instead of a default centre crop that loses the subject.

answer_sheet.Subject and placement: Keep the entire sneaker at the far left of the original. Its position within the new square is your call.
answer_sheet.Handling a tight crop: Use plain padding matching the background if necessary to keep the whole shoe.
answer_sheet.Other edits and text: No other edits and no added text.

must_haves: The output includes the original left-side sneaker, not an empty crop of the middle of the source.
The complete sneaker remains visible, including toe, heel and sole.
The sneaker's proportions, colour and details match the source.
Any added padding blends with the source background, with no text or decorative additions.

turns.text: Make this pic square for my shop. The shoe is way over on the left, so don't just crop the middle. Keep the whole shoe; plain padding to match the background is fine if needed. No other edits. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**The cheapest—and best—way is a $0 canvas resize, not an AI edit.** I haven’t run anything or spent credits.

Your image is 512 × 192 px. To make it square without losing any of the shoe:
- Keep the entire original image.
- Expand the canvas to **512 × 512 px**, adding 160 px above and below.
- Fill that padding with a plain gray sampled from the background. No cropping, stretching, or shoe edits.

You can do this free in a basic image editor. The padding may have a visible boundary because the original background isn’t perfectly uniform.

**Using the connected Magic Hour tools:** the free-plan AI editor starts at **5 credits for one 640px image**. I can’t verify an exact charge with the tools available here, and AI editing could alter details—so I don’t recommend it for your “no other edits” requirement. There’s no plain canvas-resize tool connected.

Smaller output won’t beat the **$0 manual method**, and “shorter” only applies to video. Would you like quick instructions for the free canvas method?

For the **$0 padding method**, use Photopea (free in your browser). I can’t apply a plain canvas resize through the connected tools, so **no credits have been spent**.

1. Open **photopea.com** and load your photo.
2. Choose **Image → Canvas Size**.
3. Set **Width: 512 px**, **Height: 512 px**, with the **center anchor** selected. This preserves the whole photo and shoe.
4. Use the **Eyedropper** to sample a gray from the photo’s background.
5. Add a new layer **beneath the photo**, then use **Edit → Fill → Foreground Color** to fill it with that gray.
6. Choose **File → Export As → JPG**.

The result is square, with plain padding above and below and no changes to the shoe.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.agent:
The cheapest option is the **$0 manual canvas resize**. I can’t perform that directly with the connected tools, and I haven’t spent any credits.

If you mean **“use Magic Hour to do it for me,”** that’s the AI option starting at **5 credits**, not the free method. It may also change image details. Do you want to authorize that paid-in-credits option?

Magic Hour refused the edit because the account has **insufficient credits**. No image was created and no credits were spent.

The **$0 manual padding method** is still available; there isn’t a cheaper executable option in the connected tools.
